you crashed Root cause
.venv was deleted while the gateway process (started May 10) was still running. The Python binary kept executing via mmap, but lazy open() on files inside the venv (like certifi/cacert.pem) failed → FileNotFoundError from ssl.create_default_context inside httpx, on every new AnthropicBedrock client init.
What I did
1. Recreated the venv: uv sync --frozen --all-extras (full --all-extras failed on mistralai resolver — used frozen lockfile to bypass).
2. Killed the broken process (PID 3879941) with SIGKILL after SIGTERM didn't take.
3. Relaunched in a new detached tmux session hermes-gateway (was running in a ghostty terminal scope before — would have died if you closed that window).
Status
New PID 1112071, Telegram connected, cron ticker started, 1 platform live. Logs flowing to /home/avifenesh/.hermes/logs/gateway.log.
Useful follow-ups (not done — your call)
Attach to watch it: tmux attach -t hermes-gateway (Ctrl-b d to detach)
Make this permanent: wrap it in a ~/.config/systemd/user/hermes-gateway.service so it survives reboots and auto-restarts. The tmux session won't survive a reboot.
Better error surface: the catch-all in gateway/run.py:7152 strips the file path from FileNotFoundError. Worth changing str(e)[:300] to also include getattr(e, 'filename', '') so you don't have to dig through logs next time.
--all-extras resolve failure — your lockfile's exclude-newer cutoff (2026-05-05) blocks a re-resolve when Python 3.14 is in the supported set; pre-existing issue, only bit because uv sync tried to re-resolve. --frozen sidesteps it.
